anti_overlap: fd-payments-schema-governance covers enum/versioning governance of the schema itself, not lineage/custody field design
fd-postproduction-pipeline-staging covers staged tier routing and tool handoff, not destruction-gating or audit lineage
fd-aviation-mro-compliance-record covers regulatory sign-off and retention scheduling, which is adjacent but focused on certifying-authority record permanence rather than in-pipeline custody transfer
distance_rationale: Clinical lab pipelines are a parallel discipline: a physical specimen (like raw footage) moves through a staged, multi-system pipeline (collection -> accessioning -> processing -> reporting) with strict identity/custody rules and irreversible destruction steps, but the domain is medical/regulatory rather than privacy-technical and the 'systems' are LIS/instrument interfaces rather than Swift/Python.
expected_isomorphisms: Chain-of-custody discipline — every transfer of a specimen or derived result is logged with who/what/when/hash-equivalent identifier, destruction only occurs after confirmed downstream result capture, and a specimen that never resolves goes to a manual review queue rather than silent disposal — maps directly onto raw_quarantined handling, verify-then-delete reclaim, provenance lineage fields, and the dead-letter state for stalled sessions.
focus: Provenance/lineage integrity and irreversible-destruction safety across the raw-to-derived pipeline lifecycle.
name: fd-labmed-chain-of-custody
persona: Apply the perspective of a clinical laboratory quality-systems director (CLIA/CAP-style chain-of-custody owner) — they care about whether every specimen and derived artifact has an unbroken, attributable lineage from collection to disposal; they measure the pipeline by whether an auditor can reconstruct exactly which instrument/reagent-lot/technician touched a given result; they flag any destructive step that isn't provably gated on a confirmed, checksummed downstream result.
review_areas: Whether the provenance lineage fields specified for M0 (stage versions, model checkpoints, source-artifact hashes, redaction-implementation id) are actually sufficient to answer 'which exact code path produced this derived artifact' months later, the way a lab must answer 'which reagent lot and analyzer produced this result'

Whether the contract distinguishes reversible custody transfer (e.g., artifact copied) from irreversible destruction (raw reclaim) with different guarantees for each, since conflating them is a classic chain-of-custody defect

Whether a no-op stage's conformance test actually exercises provenance-field population, or only checks input/output plumbing while leaving lineage fields an untested afterthought at this earliest, cheapest-to-fix stage

Whether the contract has a place to record a 'stage failed to confirm' or 'result indeterminate' state analogous to a lab's manual-review queue, prefiguring the dead-letter session state promised for M1-M2
Whether identifiers (sighting_id, session_id, artifact hashes) are content-addressed/immutable in a way that prevents silent identity drift as an artifact moves between the two language runtimes
Whether the schema models a single linear lineage or can express the fan-out/fan-in reality (one session producing four sinks, each with independent provenance) without losing per-sink attribution

severity_examples.condition: This directly undermines the §12 requirement that jawndex records be able to reference which redaction implementation (device Vision vs. node YOLO+SCRFD) struck each record — a lab report that can't say which analyzer ran the test is not auditable.
severity_examples.scenario: The M0 schema defines provenance lineage as a flat set of manifest-level fields with no per-sink or per-stage-invocation structure, so once garment/blur/inpainting stages all run against one session, it becomes impossible to attribute which redaction implementation touched which specific derived artifact.

severity_examples.condition: Once real stages (M2+) are built by copying the no-op skeleton, provenance population becomes a per-stage improvisation instead of a contract-enforced habit, exactly how labs that don't bake chain-of-custody into the earliest instrument interface spec end up retrofitting it under audit pressure.
severity_examples.scenario: The no-op stage skeleton and its conformance test validate only inputs/outputs/tier/privacy_class plumbing, with provenance fields left optional or unpopulated in the reference implementation.

severity_examples.condition: Ambiguous hash scope lets Swift and Python compute different hashes for logically-identical artifacts, breaking cross-language identity checks the same way inconsistent specimen-barcode formats break cross-lab result matching.
severity_examples.scenario: Content-addressing for artifacts is mentioned but the hash scope (whole file vs. logical content vs. including metadata) isn't pinned in the M0 schema.

source_domain: Clinical laboratory medicine / diagnostic specimen chain-of-custody and LIS (Laboratory Information System) interoperability
success_hints: Confirms provenance/lineage fields are structured per-stage-invocation or per-sink, not a single flat manifest blob that loses attribution once multiple stages touch a session
Confirms the no-op stage's conformance test exercises provenance-field population, not just input/output shape
Confirms content-addressing hash scope (what exactly gets hashed) is specified precisely enough for Swift and Python to agree
Notes any destructive operation should have an explicit distinct guarantee from non-destructive transfer at the schema level, even if raw-reclaim behavior itself lands after M0
task_context: Reviewing an M0 brainstorm for a JSON-Schema-first, dual-language (Swift/Python) pipeline contract that defines a manifest-level provenance lineage (stage versions, model checkpoints, artifact hashes, redaction implementation id) required by a later gap-review amendment.
